title: Advanced JavaScript Multiple Choice
description: Hoisting/TDZ, closures, higher-order functions, the prototype chain, and ES modules from module 04.

questions.explanation: `var` declarations are hoisted and auto-initialized to `undefined`, so reading `x` before its assignment is legal and prints `"undefined"`.
`let`/`const` are hoisted but stay uninitialized in the Temporal Dead Zone until their declaration line runs — reading early throws.
`count` is captured by reference inside the closure, so each `inc()` call mutates the same private variable that `get()` later reads.
Each call to the factory function creates a fresh, independent closure. Mutating `a`'s private `count` never affects `b`'s.

questions.prompt:
```js
console.log([1, 2, 3].map((n) => n * 2));
```

What is true about the result?

options.text: It is a new array `[2, 4, 6]`; the original array is unchanged
It mutates `[1, 2, 3]` in place and returns the same array
It returns `undefined` because `map` has no return value
It returns a shorter array than the input

questions.explanation: `map` always returns a new array with the same length as the input, one output per input element, and never mutates the original.
`filter` keeps only the elements where the callback returns a truthy value, producing a new (possibly shorter) array — here the two non-empty strings.

options.text: `Object.create` copies `greet` onto `child` as an own property
Calling `child.greet()` throws because `child` has no own `greet`

questions.explanation: `Object.create(proto)` links `child`'s prototype to `parent` without copying properties. `hasOwn` only checks own properties; `in` checks the whole prototype chain.

options.text: `import { default as Widget, default as version } from "./widget.js";`

questions.explanation: A default import has no braces and comes first; named imports use braces. A module can mix one default export with any number of named exports.
